The consonants which are involved are those that form the so-called square of mutes:
1. The voiceless stops, π, τ, κ, are represented in cognate English words by f, th, h.
2. The voiced stops, β, δ, γ, are represented in cognate English words by p, t, k.
¹¹ A succinct statement of these laws may be read in Webster's New International Dictionary, 2nd ed., s.vv.
